rulings.question: D1 answers FP-4; D2: FASTER after a REDUCE_LIGHT window
rulings.disposition: MODIFY (the Chief's proposal approved with three precisions)

confidence.rationale: The rule only applies the approved transitionRule to weeks the athlete executed inside the window; the number of rungs remains unquantified by evidence (as in Q06).

rulings.decisiveBasis: returnLadder.transitionRule (a rung is left only after a whole plan week at it, every session executed with no adverse or conflicting response, and the warning signs re-answered no at that week's review); D1's two quotes (DR-149 (1)); CL-1 as context. No new number.
rulings.rule: For each sport, FASTER after a REDUCE_LIGHT window is R4 then R5 only when (i) the window holds at least one whole plan week of that sport at R3 in which every prescribed session was executed with no adverse or conflicting response, (ii) that week's review answered its check with every warning sign no (an elapsed week without its check counts as not executed, NB-4), and (iii) no other session of that sport in the window was reported adverse or conflicting. Otherwise FASTER is R3, R4, R5. FASTER's R3 week is the repeat of the window's rung (I-04), so a partly executed window never gives FASTER a second R3. The return still starts only at the window-end or early check (C-Q05-1). BALANCED and CONSERVATIVE are unchanged. A window whose planned sessions of that sport were all missed is read as rest of its days (C-Q05-5 as precised in SSCTR-FF-Q3).
rulings.whereChiefIncomplete: (1) The transitionRule's unit includes that week's check, not only the executed sessions. (2) An adverse response anywhere in the window removes the shortcut. (3) Without an explicit bar, applying the I-04 prepend on top of the new rule would give FASTER R3, R3, R4, equal to BALANCED.

rulings.question: D3 resolves NB-2; QRE-V1CPR-05 and -09; I-17; C-2 as modified; C-Q05-3
rulings.disposition: MODIFY ((a) widened to the Situation 2 restart; (b)-(e) approved with precisions; the window-opening ASK becomes non-blocking; C-2 as modified in the recheck is withdrawn)

confidence.rationale: The mapping uses the ladder's own evidence unit and S06's graded-return principle; no study tells when a race is compatible after a short reduction, so the rule errs toward not prescribing it while leaving the athlete free to take part.

rulings.decisiveBasis: Founder D3 (DR-149 (3); PCG R-RACE-1: keep means D3's keep at both questions, and the SSCTR maps compatibility and the coach's recommendation); CL-5; CL-1; probe p4.

rule.a_scope: In scope: a race (role RACE) dated from a Situation 1 window's start until that episode's running ladder completes (window, wait, R1-R4 rungs or a MODERATE recipe step, repeats and shifts included), for an episode that affects RUNNING; and a race dated inside a Situation 2 readiness restart while its running return is in force (run mode RETURN or RESTART from the declaration). A strength-only episode never involves the race (QRE-V1CPR-09). Outside the scope the race follows the event rules.
rule.b_composition: In scope the coach never plans the race at race effort or as a completion, nor the race week's race-effort touch. The race slot takes the operation the rung (or the restart week) applies to a hard session: R0 or WAIT, no session; R1, the optional walk; R2, R3, R4, a recipe step or a restart week, an easy run at the week's easy duration; on a race date that is not one of the athlete's run days, no session. The race-week touch runs easy. Race day keeps no strength. The R6 completion race day and its EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING item are not produced in scope. The event stays on the calendar as the athlete's own event: taking part is the athlete's decision, and the coach's recommendation for that day is the rung's session.
rule.c_noBlockingQuestion: No race question blocks. The window opens at once, and the return starts at the window-end or early check. Each decision that puts a race into the scope (the report, the check, a date change, a ladder repeat or shift, a goal change) carries one non-blocking offer of the three paths: keep it as your own event (the default; nothing to answer), move it (EVENT_DATE_CHANGE), or remove it (GOAL_CHANGE with no event). The offer is made when the race enters the scope, never at every decision. 'End the reduction before it' is no longer a race path: the window's days are the athlete's choice and an early end is D4's act (PCG R-RACE-1). Because (b) is a composition rule, it holds on every route that places the race in scope, which closes QRE-V1CPR-05 by construction.
rule.d_afterTheRace: Nothing of the pre-race held start passes the race (I-17). A ladder or restart week that starts after the race day takes no fixed or repeated start from before the race: it is composed from the plan's own post-race start (POST_EVENT, NEXT_BLOCK), with the rung's operation still applied until the ladder completes. A week in which a sport has only optional sessions is not a ladder week for that sport (SSCTR-V1CPI-05 (3)).
rule.e_raceExecuted: A race reported executed while in scope follows the post-event rules (the post-race eligibility check, D04). An adverse or conflicting response asks the episode's check with the exercise-response items (C-Q05-4). The race moves the ladder only through the transitionRule, is never read as evidence of readiness, and never replaces the held reference (loadReference).
rule.windowOpeningAsk: APPROVE: it becomes the non-blocking offer of (c).
rule.raceDayCompletion: Relevant. Inside the scope it is superseded by (b): a recipe step or a restart in race week would otherwise plan a completion (p4: 75 min after 15-min runs). Outside F08, after a declared nonclinical break's R6 return in race week, it is unchanged here (SSCTR D43 and D47, approved in R7-D, on the FREEZE-6 default path, not a named blocker). Whether D3 also governs that path is a PCG reading, routed non-blocking.

rulings.whereChiefWrong: (a) omits the Situation 2 restart: probe p4 prescribes a 75-min completion race in the restart's third week after 15-min runs, which D3 ('retomada incompatível') and DR-148 (5) ('the restart stays conservative') exclude. C-2 as modified in the recheck ('Keep: the return ends before the race week') is withdrawn: under D3, keeping the date never ends or shortens a return (DR-149 (3); PCG F01). C-2 still describes a race outside the scope.
conditions: C-FF2-1: The race row keeps the event's identity and date (visible, never dropped or relabelled). A derived flag marks it as the athlete's own event with the coach's recommendation. No collected field is needed; if Product records the athlete's decision to take part, Security/G07 rule on that field.

C-FF2-2: For a systemic condition the copy says the coach does not plan a race while the athlete is unwell (C-Q05-3; G03, with the warning-sign wording waiting on G04); never 'cleared' or 'safe to race'.
C-FF2-3: The RACE_DURING_RETURN disclosure (O-R1) is replaced by the offer in (c).
C-FF2-4: When the ladder (or the restart's running return) completes before the race, the race returns to the event rules, and that decision says so.

rulings.question: D4 adjusts RC-16; C-3: early end of a reduction

confidence.rationale: S06 reports that most mild infections resolve within 1-3 days and that the return is graded on responses; the early end changes only when the return starts, never its doses.

rulings.decisiveBasis: D4 (DR-149 (4); RC-16 r2 ends the day-3 interim of C-3); CL-1; the existing speed rows. No new number.
rulings.rule: An early end is the window-end check answered before the chosen end, on any day after the report day: every item of the condition's instrument actively answered (the warning signs; the exercise-response items when sessions were executed since the last check), the current eligibility screen (a current clinical flag routes clinical; a missing screen is ASK, as at the window's end, O-4), and resolved or clearly improved true. The window then lasted from its start to the day before the check, so at least the report day. At a weekly review inside the window, the same answer ends the window at the end of the reviewed plan week: the window's rung holds the remaining days of that week, and the return starts the next plan week. 'Not improved' before the chosen end changes nothing; any yes routes the clinical hold. The early end never lifts a restriction, held sport or eligibility flag in force, never resets the per-sport 14-day count, and is never a clearance. Speeds come from the days the window lasted, with the existing rows.
rulings.shortWindows: No change to the speed rows for 1- or 2-day windows. They fall in the rows up to 10 days, every speed still climbs through at least one executed week below the held doses, and a first ladder week that starts mid-week repeats (I-02). One precision: C-Q05-5 reads a REDUCE window as rest only when it held planned sessions of that sport and none was executed. When it held no planned session of that sport (common in a 1-2 day window), that sport follows its intent's row as chosen. Today executionOf reads an empty set as none executed, which adds an artificial R2 week.
rulings.whereChiefIncomplete: Two additions: the early end needs the current eligibility screen, as the window-end check does; and the weekly-review form ends the window at the end of the reviewed week, not on the review day, so no unplanned days open before the next plan week.
conditions: C-FF3-1: The improvement answer is the existing instrument's answer, not a new item; Security confirms its early use (C-Q05-8).

A 2-day early end: the speeds read the up-to-10-days row.
Weekly review inside the window answering improved: the window ends with that plan week, and the return starts the next plan week as whole weeks.

rulings.question: D6: is there an admissible lever that makes the Demanding coach prescribe differently?
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (internal analysis of the approved envelope; P5 stays INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)

confidence.rationale: Every choice point in the code either belongs to the athlete (offers), to another axis (speed, volume, difficulty), or is a lexicographic safety ranking whose alternatives a profile could only make worse or leave unchanged.

examined: Offers: graduation (B0-C01) is applied unless declined, for every profile; ladder steps (B0-C07) are 'offered (never applied)'. Both are the athlete's choice and evidence-gated. Applying a ladder step by default for DEMANDING would change an approved agency condition (B0-C07; DR-125), so it is not an authorized alternative.
Return ladder steps and Situation 2 options: the speed axis (D2), never the profile (RC-12).

Arrangement choice: choose() ranks admissible arrangements by safety, essential stimulus, interference and change cost. A profile override could only pick a higher-interference or higher-cost arrangement, or an equivalent one with no dose change.
Exercise selection: the DR-134 structure and the skill ladders (athlete agency, B0-C07).
Quality family: fixed by phase, goal and familiarity (threshold ladder, event-specific ladders, B0-C02 held exactly); no week offers an alternative.
Missed or unavailable session: a move already wins over a skip when it is admissible; catch-up is never admissible.

Gates: ADVANCE and EARNED are evidence-gated, and relaxing them is a faster progression without support (P5 rejected). The strength step order is fixed by the goal dose (for example REPS_THEN_LOAD); another order would be a new progression strategy with no evidence in this record.
rulings.limitation: No lever changes DEMANDING's prescriptions observably and admissibly. In every state (sessions, doses, gates, caps, returns, event phases, F08 paths) DEMANDING prescribes exactly what BALANCED prescribes. Its only observable differences are P4's recommendation 'ACCEPT' on the RUN_QUALITY_INTRODUCED disclosure and on LADDER_STEP offers, and the COACH_DEMANDING disclosure. It is not functionally complete as a distinct prescriptive coach in V1, and it must not be presented as distinct prescriptive behaviour (D6, DR-149 (6)). Whether it is shown at all, and how, is the Founder's and Product/UX's choice within that limit.
conditions: C-FF4-1: The advice stays non-pressuring, declining is never penalized, and the offer stays evidence-gated (DR-125, Q09 P4 conditions).
C-FF4-2: The disclosure keeps saying the doses and limits are the balanced coach's.

The recommendation appears only on LADDER_STEP offers and RUN_QUALITY_INTRODUCED.

rulings.question: QRE-V1CPR-10, RC-06: the 'choose at most 0 days' question

confidence.rationale: The rule follows the decided persistence route and the Founder's 14-day bound; it adds no number.

rulings.decisiveBasis: RC-06 and RC-16 r2 (the 14-day upper bound per sport); warningSignInstrument.persistence; PCG R-RC06-RC07-1 (per-sport count from the first window start of the chain); CL-4.
rulings.rule: Per sport, the remaining allowance is 14 minus the days from the first window start of that sport's chain to the day before the new report's start. A report that covers a sport with no day left is persistence. It takes the strictest not-improved route among the conditions of that sport's chain and the new report: the clinical hold with the professional-assessment recommendation, unless every one of them is NEED_REST, which takes the declared break or a new plan while the sessions keep waiting. Warning signs and the current screen are read first. When every covered sport has days left, the days question offers 1 to the smallest remaining allowance among the covered sports, as a continuation of the chain: the chain already holds the reduction, and D4 makes the 3-14 days a choice, not a minimum. No question ever offers 0 days.
rulings.whereChiefIncomplete: 'The chain condition's not-improved route' is ambiguous when the new report names another condition: the strictest route among the chain's conditions and the new one applies. The count is per sport, so the smallest allowance bounds a report that covers several sports.
directedTests: QRE scenario: NEED_REST REST 10 days from week 1 Monday, no check; week 3 Tuesday UNUSUAL_FATIGUE REST 3 days: CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED (professional assessment), recorded; no days question.
NEED_REST REST 10 days, no check; week 3 Tuesday NEED_REST again: the NEED_REST route (declared break or new plan); the sessions keep waiting.
MILD_ILLNESS REST 10 days, no check; a new UNUSUAL_FATIGUE report on day 12: the days question offers 1 to 3; the answer 3 runs the window to day 14, and its check follows.
A remaining allowance of 1 offers exactly 1.
A report covering RUN (2 days left) and STRENGTH (no chain): the question offers 1 to 2.
No reason text anywhere offers 'at most 0 days'.

rulings.question: C-1 as modified, for the Engineering of NB-1: readings (i)-(vii); also Security OBS-R2
rulings.disposition: MODIFY ((i)-(v) corrected, (vi) approved per sport, (vii) answered yes); the chaining rule CH-r2 below states C-1 as modified for implementation

confidence.rationale: Each rule follows from 'never less conservative than any report', RC-13 and S06's persistence and recurrence content. The combination logic is internal and unvalidated, and it errs toward the stricter reading.

rulings.decisiveBasis: C-1 as modified (recheck), RC-06, RC-07, RC-13, Q05 (systemic coverage, illness ceiling, holds), C-Q05-1, C-Q05-2, warningSignInstrument.persistence, CL-4 (S06 Table 4 recurrence cell), PCG R-RC06-RC07-1; code facts: an R0-R3 operation is applied to the week's start state, which is the held pre-window state at R-rungs and the recipe's own state at an M step.

readings.i: CORRECTED. A MODERATE recipe step (M) ranks with R4, not as R2 or R3. It is the recipe's own state with no rung operation, and any R0-R3 operation applied on top of that state is never above it. Ranking the entry as R2 would let an R2 report raise running from the 15-min recipe runs to the week's easy duration; ranking later steps as R3 would let an R3 report ('reduce the difficulty') keep strength at RIR 3. Order: R0 = WAIT > R1 > R2 > R3 > R4 = M.
readings.ii: CORRECTED. 'Equal keeps its episode' would let a systemic or illness report at the same rung miss a sport (the SSCTR-V1CPI-01 class). Only an equal or lighter report of the same condition, inside that condition's window, keeps the episode unchanged (CH-r2-3 (b)). Any other report moves the covered sport at the more restrictive of the two rungs, carrying the unresolved conditions (CH-r2-3 (c)). A covered sport no episode governs joins the new report.
readings.iii: CORRECTED. The moved sport carries every condition not yet answered resolved or clearly improved, not only illness-type ones (an unresolved UNUSUAL_FATIGUE or MINOR_DISCOMFORT would otherwise lose its check and persistence). Each carried condition keeps its own chosen end, items and persistence route. The illness ceiling holds while an illness-type condition is carried.
readings.iv: CORRECTED. One check per review answers every open episode with the union of the unresolved conditions' items. 'Improved' is asked per condition, at or after its own end or earlier by the athlete's choice. A single answer covering every condition would route a NEED_REST still unresolved plus an improved discomfort to the clinical hold, or would release a sport while one of its conditions is unresolved.
readings.v: CORRECTED. 'Lighter opens nothing, nothing recorded, not persistence' applies only to the same condition inside its window (the -06 case, where the check is D4's early end). A lighter report of another condition is bound to the sport and recorded.
readings.vi: APPROVED, per sport (PCG R-RC06-RC07-1): each sport's count runs from the first window start of its chain; an early end or a declared break never resets it; it resets only after a whole ladder week of that sport has been executed after the chain's last window (every prescribed session executed with no adverse or conflicting response, and the week's review answered with its check). An episode on a disjoint sport neither resets nor extends it.
readings.vii: YES. A report that covers only sports no episode governs opens its own episode and its own chain; this removes the I-06 limitation for disjoint sports (B4, RC-13). A report on the same sport with a different strength region merges into the whole sport at the more restrictive rung, carrying the other region's unresolved condition; this removes the I-06 ASK as well. Conservative, and the early end mitigates it.

chainingRule: CH-r2-1: Clinical first: the warning signs (any yes routes the clinical hold for every sport) and today's eligibility screen, unchanged.
CH-r2-2: Per sport at most one episode governs. Restrictiveness: R0 = WAIT > R1 > R2 > R3 > R4 = M.

CH-r2-3: For each sport the report covers: (a) no episode governs it: it joins the new report's window; (b) the report names the same condition as every unresolved condition bound to the sport, its rung is equal to or lighter than the rung in force, and it ends on or before the sport's window end: nothing changes for that sport (KEEP, with the check offered, which is D4's early end; no WELLBEING_DECLARED row for it; not persistence); (c) otherwise the sport moves to the new report's window at the more restrictive of the new rung and the rung in force, carrying every condition bound to it not yet answered resolved or clearly improved.
CH-r2-4: A sport the report does not cover keeps its episode, window, wait or ladder and its own check (C-1 modified (a)).

CH-r2-5: While a sport carries several conditions, its rung on a day is the most restrictive among the carried windows running that day, and WAIT for a carried condition past its own end with no improvement answer. The illness ceiling (R2, R1 or R0) holds while an illness-type condition is carried. The sport's gates hold (Q05).

CH-r2-6: One check per review covers every open episode: the union of the unresolved conditions' items, the exercise-response items when sessions were executed since the last check, and 'improved' asked per condition (at or after its own end, or earlier by the athlete's choice). Each answer applies to its condition. Before its own end, 'not improved' changes nothing. At or after its end, 'not improved' takes that condition's persistence route.

CH-r2-7: A sport's return starts when every condition bound to it is answered improved. Its speed row reads the most restrictive rung the sport held in its chain's windows (R0 or R1: the REST/LIGHT rows; R2: REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL; R3: REDUCE_LIGHT; C-Q05-5 as precised in SSCTR-FF-Q3). For the REST/LIGHT rows it also reads the sport's R0/R1 days plus its waited days (SSCTR-FF-N1). The speed is the athlete's latest choice.

CH-r2-8: The same condition after its own end. In its WAIT (no improvement answer yet), a report of that condition is the not-improved answer: persistence route, no new window (RC-06). After it was answered improved and before the chain resets, a report of that condition is a recurrence: it takes that condition's persistence route (the clinical hold with the professional-assessment recommendation; NEED_REST: the declared break or a new plan). Basis: CL-4 (S06: symptoms that initially improve and then recur indicate severe or complicated infection, whose return is under professional care). This answers Security OBS-R2: the original report counts. It replaces C-Q05-2's 'hold the rung that week, assessment at the next report' for recurrences; inside the window, adjustments within the bound remain allowed (CH-r2-3).
CH-r2-9: The 14-day count per sport follows (vi). A report covering a sport with no day left is persistence (SSCTR-FF-Q6); otherwise the days question offers 1 to the smallest remaining allowance.

CH-r2-10: Every report except case 3 (b) is recorded, append-only. A superseded marker ends from the report's day and keeps its history. Supersession is never a conversion between a report and a break (RC-07), and nothing is relabelled (R-F08-1).
directedTests: V1CPR-01 (a): MILD_ILLNESS REST 7 days for both sports; MINOR_DISCOMFORT RUN REDUCE_LIGHT 3 days: running stays at R0, carrying the illness; strength keeps the illness window; the illness check (W1-W15 and improved) is due at its end; no strength step in week 5.

V1CPR-01 (b): MILD_ILLNESS return at R2 (illness improved); MINOR_DISCOMFORT RUN REDUCE_LIGHT 3 days: running moves to the discomfort window at R2; strength keeps R2, R3, R4; no strength above R2 in week 6; running returns on the REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL row.

V1CPR-01 (c): MINOR_DISCOMFORT return at R2 for both sports; NEED_REST STRENGTH REST 3 days: strength moves to R0; running keeps R2, then R3, then R4, never the held doses plus a step after the R2 week.

V1CPR-01 (d): MILD_ILLNESS REST window; UNUSUAL_FATIGUE REDUCE_LIGHT for both sports: both sports stay at R0 until the illness's end, carrying both conditions; W11 and W15 are still asked; at an R2 rung a REDUCE_LIGHT report of another condition keeps R2 (never 1 set raised to 3).

V1CPR-01 (e): MILD_ILLNESS REST 10 days; early end on day 3; the next day MILD_ILLNESS REST 14 days: a recurrence, CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with the professional-assessment recommendation; never 18 days of windows.
-06: the same condition, lighter, inside the window: KEEP with the check offered, no WELLBEING_DECLARED row, not persistence; the same report the next week inside the window: still KEEP.
The same condition reported in its WAIT: its not-improved route (MINOR_DISCOMFORT and illness: clinical; NEED_REST: declared break or new plan); no new window.

M step: a REDUCE_LIGHT report of another condition on a sport at a recipe step moves it to R3 applied on the recipe's state (strength 1 set at RIR 4 or more from 2 sets at RIR 3; the long run never above the recipe's); after the window the recipe continues from its state.
Disjoint sports: MINOR_DISCOMFORT RUN open; a new MINOR_DISCOMFORT STRENGTH: its own episode, no ASK; separate checks, ladders and counts.
Regions: MINOR_DISCOMFORT STRENGTH UPPER at R3; a new STRENGTH LOWER report at R2: whole-body strength at R2, carrying the upper condition.

Per-condition improvement: NEED_REST (running) improved and MINOR_DISCOMFORT (strength) not improved at their ends: the discomfort's clinical route. NEED_REST not improved and discomfort improved: the NEED_REST route for running, and strength returns.
Count per sport: an early end does not reset it; a declared break does not reset it; a whole executed and reviewed ladder week resets it; a disjoint episode neither resets nor extends it.
OBS-R2: an original MILD_ILLNESS report in week 1, improved in week 2, the same condition in week 3 before the reset: recurrence, clinical route.

confidence.rationale: The self-inclusion rule is closed and elliptical, so long ordinary clauses cannot trigger it; the residual is self-report and unlisted wording.

rulings.rule: In a reason whose clauses hold at least one third-party clinical mention (an OTHER clause with a clinical word, phrase or damage mention), a clause is SELF_INCLUSION when, after dropping at most two leading conjunctions, every token belongs to the closed classes below, the clause holds an anchor (a first-person pronoun or first-person verb form), it holds an additive, a pronoun object or a contagion verb, and it holds no negator. A SELF_INCLUSION clause makes every third-party clinical mention of that reason the athlete's own (CLINICAL). A clause made only of additives, conjunctions and fillers, with no anchor ('same', 'too', 'also', 'tbm', 'também', 'también', 'igual', 'idem'), is UNCERTAIN: ASK, and the structured clinicalReason no does not resolve it (new basis SELF_INCLUSION_UNCERTAIN; its exit is restating the note or answering yes). An exclusion ('not me', 'I didn't get it', 'eu não', 'yo no') leaves the mention third-party. The existing ELLIPSES list stays as regression data. Every other rule of Q01 is unchanged; free text still only adds CLINICAL or ASK.

rulings.question: D5: the potentially serious sign set for urgent-care guidance
rulings.disposition: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS (the set W2, W3, W4, W5 and X1 confirmed from S06; X4 stays at professional assessment)

confidence.rationale: S06 names these symptoms as indicators of possible cardiac or lower-respiratory involvement and links cardiac complications to adverse events during return. The source itself grades no urgency, so the urgent level is the Founder's interim decision mapped onto the source's most serious category, pending G04.

rulings.decisiveBasis: CL-2 (S06 Table 4 'Severe / complicated: symptoms indicating other organ involvement e.g. cardiac (chest pain, pressure or tightness, dizziness, palpitations / racing heart, shortness of breath)', footnote b; section 4 on myocarditis/pericarditis and adverse events during return); CL-3; S06 Table 7 and Checklist 3 (the same cardiorespiratory symptoms during or after exercise); D5 (DR-149 (5)).
rulings.rule: The runtime returns a structured guidance level with every clinical route caused by a warning sign or an exercise-response item: URGENT_CARE_ADVISED when any item answered yes is W2 (chest pain, pressure or tightness), W3 (shortness of breath or fast breathing at rest), W4 (palpitations or a racing heart at rest), W5 (fainting, near-fainting or dizziness) or X1 (unusual breathlessness, chest pain or discomfort, dizziness or a racing heart during or after exercise); otherwise PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT. The level is marked INTERIM_PENDING_G04. It is derived only from the items answered yes: no combination logic, no diagnosis label, no new collected field. Persistence (not improved), a recurrence, a clinical reason or category, an eligibility flag and pain with a substitution carry PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT. An unanswered item is ASK and carries no level. Situation 2 declarations and checks use the same mapping.
rulings.x4: X4 (very dark brown or red urine after exercise) stays PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT. S06 groups it with the symptoms that call for consulting a medical doctor; the record-only rhabdomyolysis guidance stratifies risk (CL-7). Whether X4 warrants an urgent level is a G04 question; its copy must not be weaker than 'stop and seek a medical assessment'.
rulings.w5: W5 is compound (Security keeps compound items compound). S06 lists dizziness among the cardiac-involvement indicators, so the item maps to URGENT_CARE_ADVISED. The copy states urgency in proportion (fainting versus light-headedness) as wording, not as a new item (G03, G04).
rulings.notUrgent: W1, W6-W15, X2-X4, persistence and every non-sign route: PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT. Mild indisposition is never presented as an emergency (D5).
rulings.whereChiefIncomplete: The set is right. Three additions: the level is derived only from the items answered yes; a multi-item answer takes the higher level; and X4 is recorded as a G04 question rather than silently excluded.
conditions: C-FF9-1: Copy is G03 and G04, marked for review before real use; no invented diagnosis, urgency class or clearance; never 'emergency' for persistence or mild indisposition.
C-FF9-2: Security confirms that the derived level adds no collected data and stays out of logs and outbound surfaces (SEC-V1CP-09, 15-18).
C-FF9-3: FUTURE_G04_REVALIDATION of the set and the wording.
directedTests: Each of W2, W3, W4, W5 and X1 answered yes alone, at entry, at a check, at an S6 declaration and after an adverse session: the clinical route with URGENT_CARE_ADVISED and INTERIM_PENDING_G04.
Each of W1, W6-W15, X2, X3 and X4 alone: PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT.
W7 and W2 together: URGENT_CARE_ADVISED.

newFindings.title: The return after a window ignores the days the athlete waited for the check
newFindings.found: by this instance while ruling FF-Q3 and FF-Q7 (probe p2); pre-existing at 5ee9dec, not among NB-1..NB-6
newFindings.location: CoachingCore/src/r6-adaptation.mjs:1122 returnPlans and :1102 speedPlan read only the window's days
newFindings.scenario: MILD_ILLNESS REST 3 days; the check 16 days later (3 window days and 13 waited days without training): FASTER R3 then R4 (easy 35, long 35-50, strength 1 then 2 sets), the same as a check at the window's end. The R6 classes call for the MODERATE recipe after 16 days without training (15-min entry runs, then conditional steps).
newFindings.expected: A combination of the two paths is never less conservative than either (the principle of SSCTR-V1CPI-03 and I-15): per sport, days without training are days without training.
newFindings.rule: For the return's row, the days a sport waited for the window-end check (from the day after the window's end to the day before the check) are days without training. (a) After a REST or LIGHT_ACTIVITY_ONLY window the row reads the window's days plus the waited days: up to shortMaxDays (10) the rows up to 10 days; 11 to moderateMaxDays (28) the 11-14 rows (the MODERATE recipe with the speed's holds); beyond moderateMaxDays the R6 LONG class (restart from current capacity, prior doses only as a ceiling) at every speed. (b) After a REDUCE window, up to shortMaxDays of waited days leave the row as chosen: the window's rung already starts a climb that is never less conservative than the R6 SHORT resume. More than shortMaxDays of waited days read the window as a REST window of those waited days, then as (a). No new number: the existing R6 class bounds are applied to the same quantity.
directedTests: REST 3 days and a check 9 days later (12 days without training): FASTER plans the MODERATE recipe, not R3 then R4.
REST 3 days and a check the day after the window: unchanged.
REDUCE_LIGHT 3 days and 5 waited days: the REDUCE_LIGHT row, unchanged.
REDUCE_LIGHT 3 days and 12 waited days: the MODERATE recipe.
REST 5 days and 30 waited days: the R6 LONG class at every speed.

otherSportingNotes: SB-1 (SEC-V1CPI-02 residual, RC-11 matching rule, routed to SSCTR and PCG): a readiness declaration answers the hold it was made for. Executed training after it ends that coverage, so a later stop is a new interruption whose reason is screened and, when missing, asked (SSCTR-05: an unexplained interruption is never assumed nonclinical). The interim fail-closed ASK is also the sporting rule.

The completion race day of an R6 nonclinical return (RETURN_IN_RACE_WEEK) outside F08 is unchanged here. A future SSCTR item could weigh its single-session size against the return's runs; it is not a blocker of this mission.
engineeringRules: ER-1 (FF-Q1): FASTER after REDUCE_LIGHT is [R4] only with a whole executed R3 plan week inside the window, reviewed with its check, and no adverse session in the window; otherwise [R3, R4], with no extra prepend.

ER-2 (FF-Q2 a, b): in scope (an F08 episode affecting running until its running ladder completes; a Situation 2 restart while its running return is in force), the RACE row takes the rung's operation for a hard session, or no session on a non-run day; RACE_TOUCH is eased at R4 and M too; strength stays off race day; no completion prescription and no EVENT_AMBITIOUS item; the event stays visible and is flagged as the athlete's own.
ER-3 (FF-Q2 c): no race ASK at the report, at the check or on any route; one non-blocking offer (keep as default, move, remove) when the race enters the scope.

ER-4 (FF-Q2 d): ladder or restart weeks after the race day take no fixed or repeated pre-race start; they use the plan's own post-race start with the rung's operation; a sport with only optional sessions in a week does not count it as a ladder week.

ER-5 (FF-Q3): an early end from the day after the report day, with the current screen; at a weekly review it takes effect at the end of that plan week; F08_MIN_DAYS goes; a REDUCE window with no planned session of a sport follows its intent's row.
ER-6 (FF-Q6): per-sport allowance; no day left gives the strictest persistence route; otherwise offer 1 to the smallest allowance; never 0.
ER-8 (FF-Q8): lexicon V1CP-A1-LEX-3 and the SELF_INCLUSION and UNCERTAIN rule.
ER-9 (FF-Q9): guidanceLevel on clinical routes from signs: URGENT_CARE_ADVISED for W2-W5 and X1, otherwise PROFESSIONAL_ASSESSMENT, marked INTERIM_PENDING_G04.
ER-10 (N1, if included): waited days count toward the return's row with the existing R6 class bounds.
Every rule: the default path (no F08 report) stays byte-identical to the reviewed baseline (C-Q12-4, CF-2); RED on 5ee9dec, GREEN after.

aeReview.answer: Current plan adequate? The default path is unchanged. The rulings act only on F08 paths (reports, checks, waits, races inside a return, restarts) and on the lexicon; DEMANDING is unchanged.
Material fact with provenance? Every rule reads structured, recorded facts: reports, checks, executed sessions, race dates, declarations. Free text only raises (RC-05).

Is KEEP defensible? KEEP stays where nothing material changed (a same-condition report inside the window; a race kept as the athlete's own event). Unknowns: the athlete's response to a race they choose to run, lexicon coverage.

Is change necessary, against 5ee9dec? Yes: a race prescribed at race effort or as a completion inside a return (p4), a return blind to waited days (p2), chained reports that drop a sport's protection (SSCTR-V1CPR-01), self-inclusion misses (p3).
Smallest sufficient intervention? Composition rules that reuse the existing rung operations, recipes and R6 classes; no new dose.

Why not smaller alternatives? Disclosing the race leaves a prescription D3 excludes. Asking blocks eligible training (D3). Ignoring waited days leaves the F08 return less conservative than R6 for the same days. 'Equal keeps' leaves a systemic report off one sport.
Does the trade-off protect priority and progression? Returns stay evidence-conditioned, the race stays the athlete's, and progression resumes through the transitionRule.

Does evidence support conclusion and dose? S06 supports the direction (graded return, consulting on symptoms, cardiac indicators, recurrence) with limits (respiratory infections, expert opinion, elite focus). No dose is new.

Material uncertainty? Extrapolation of S06 beyond respiratory infections; the unquantified number of rungs; the lexicon's coverage; X4's level; whether athletes keep reporting with stricter recurrence routing (product data).

ASK, HOLD or CLINICAL? Clinical routes for warning signs, persistence and recurrence (professional assessment; the readiness declaration is the way back). ASK only for an unanswered item or an uncertain self-inclusion; never for a race.

expiry.eventBasedExpiry: Any change to DR-149, PCG-V1CPFF-F08-r1 or DR-148; the implementation of these rules (judged by a fresh SSCTR instance); a G04 owner; funded human revalidation; an adverse event; a new consensus on return after illness; product data on returns, races during returns or recurrences. A stale decision does not extend silently.
